attempts.label: CRCNS:hc-7
attempts.entry_title: Inhibitory synaptic dynamics of CA3 PV+ and CCK+ interneurons (Kohus et al. 2016)
attempts.summary: The paper's main findings on short-term plasticity largely held up here: uIPSC kinetics and amplitude differ by presynaptic cell type, PV+ interneuron synapses depress more at higher frequencies, and CCK+ synapses facilitate during short bursts. The late onset of asynchronous release at CCK+ synapses did not reproduce, likely because the paper does not describe its onset rule and the rules tried also flag PV+ pairs the paper calls synchronous. CCK+ basket cell to pyramidal cell trains facilitated in only 1 of 6 pairs, and the plasticity models reproduced in part. The interneuron firing clusters, connection probabilities, spontaneous IPSCs and sharp-wave ripple results could not be tested, as those recordings are not in the dataset.
attempts.description: Tests the paired-recording findings of Kohus, Kali, Rovira-Esteban, Schlingloff, Papp, Freund, Hajos and Gulyas (2016) on CRCNS data set hc-7, which holds the raw sweeps and the authors' amplitude and success tables of 60 interneuron to pyramidal cell and interneuron pairs under trains, RIP, EPI and recovery protocols. It compares uIPSC kinetics between connection types, short-term plasticity, recovery, asynchronous release and the fits of four short-term plasticity models. The current-step, connectivity, spontaneous IPSC and field potential data of the paper are not in the data set.

With the single AP 1.3 s before the RIP burst (M3 a), all five measures differ across PV+BC (7 pairs), AAC (7) and CCK+BC (12) to PC pairs at p < 0.05, with the authors' failures (M2 a; rise 0.0191, latency 0.00842, amplitude 0.00405, potency 0.00624, transmission probability 0.00951) and with detected failures (M2 b; 0.00653 to 0.0179). The 1 Hz train (M3 b; 4, 3 and 3 pairs) gives no difference and the pooled reading (M3 c) three or four. The decay time constant does not differ (p 0.122). Medians (M3 a, M2 a) PV+BC, AAC, CCK+BC; rise 0.601, 0.547, 0.709 ms; latency 0.747, 0.664, 0.999 ms; amplitude 113.1, 226.1, 40.3 pA; transmission probability 1.0, 1.0, 0.875. With only the 6 CCK+BC to PC pairs at or below the type's median holding current, rise and latency no longer differ (p 0.26 and 0.14, against 0.021 and 0.0084 with all 12 pairs, on the per-pair table of the pipette check), so these two differences depend on the pairs where a CsCl admixture would lengthen latency; with 6 pairs the tests also lose power.
deviations: The data set holds 7 PV+BC, 8 AAC (7 with a RIP recording) and 12 CCK+BC to PC pairs, against the paper's 8, 9 and 14 high KCl pairs.
Rise, latency and peak are measured on averaged sweeps with a baseline 4 to 0.8 ms before the AP peak and a response window 0.3 to 8 ms after it, standard choices the paper does not give.

The files do not say which pipette solution each pair was recorded with. Assumed that every IN to PC pair is a high KCl pair, as no type has more pairs than the paper's high KCl count and the paper says most pairs were recorded with it (Methods, paired recordings). Checked per pair in the notebook (holding current, rise time and latency by recording day); no type splits into two groups (holding currents -376.0 to 23.4 pA, spread continuously), but a mixture with CsCl pairs cannot be ruled out, and CsCl lengthens rise time and latency (Results, Fig. 7). In CCK+BC to PC pairs latency rises with the holding current (rho 0.58, p 0.048), one sign against the assumption.

outcomes.notes: At most 4 of the 8 comparisons hold, under M3 a with either M2 reading; AAC against CCK+BC for rise time, latency, amplitude and potency (Bonferroni-corrected p 0.0293, 0.0157, 0.0112, 0.0157). PV+BC against CCK+BC goes the stated way for rise time, latency and amplitude but misses the corrected threshold (0.205, 0.0512, 0.0663; uncorrected 0.0683, 0.0171, 0.0221). AAC against CCK+BC transmission probability gives corrected p 0.159. The 1 Hz reading gives 0 of 8 and the pooled reading 2 of 8. The criterion's partial threshold is five comparisons.
deviations: Fewer pairs than the paper (7, 7 and 12 against 8, 9 and 14), which lowers the power of the post hoc tests; all pairs treated as high KCl pairs.

outcomes.notes: The data set holds 7 CCK+DTI to PC pairs. Three have no RIP recording and are marked "No release" for RIP in Experiments_description.txt; they are counted as silent (3 of 7, 43%, against the 85% the criterion requires). The other four transmit to the single AP before RIP (success rates 0.55 to 0.85 under M2 a; detection rates 0.50 to 0.95 against 0.20 to 0.50 with no AP under M2 b). All seven transmit to the single AP after an EPI train under M2 a, six under M2 b. Transmission builds up over the sweeps; none of the four succeeds in the first sweep, the only single AP not preceded by a RIP burst 1600 ms earlier (Methods, protocols paragraph). Counting a pair as silent when it fails in sweeps 1 to 3 gives 5 of 7 (71%), and in the first sweep 7 of 7. The criterion counts any success in any sweep; whether it should count the first sweeps is asked of a reader (questions/crcns-hc-7.yaml). The paper's own later statement that four of eight pairs respond at 1 to 40 Hz or to RIP agrees better with these data.
deviations: 7 pairs where the paper reports 8; pairs without a RIP recording are taken as silent from the authors' "No release" label.

outcomes.notes: The pairs are not labelled by pipette solution, in the files, the headers, the descriptor or Experiments_description.txt, so CsCl pairs cannot be told from high KCl pairs. The pair counts (7, 8, 12 to PC) do not exceed the paper's high KCl counts, which suggests the CsCl pairs were not deposited, but the data do not show it.

Under M4 b with the Wilcoxon reading of the test the PV+BC medians at the 3rd and 4th AP are 0.372 and 0.329 (p 0.0156, 7 pairs) and the AAC median at the 2nd AP 0.679 (p 0.0312, 7 pairs). Under M4 a it holds only with the Mann-Whitney reading (PV+BC 0.650 and 0.641, p 0.00106; AAC 0.767, p 0.0204); with the Wilcoxon test the AAC 2nd AP misses (p 0.109). The Mann-Whitney reading compares the values with a constant vector of ones and gives p 0.00106 whenever all 7 lie on one side of 1, so it is degenerate; this is asked of a reader, and the outcome does not rest on it. The PV+BC 2nd AP is not depressed (1.15 under M4 a, 0.969 under M4 b, p 0.172 or more).
deviations: The RIP bursts in the data are at 222 Hz (4.5 ms between APs), not the 160 Hz of the paper.

outcomes.notes: Both onset rules of the criterion were run. Rule (a), immediate asynchronous charge above 2 SD of the baseline charge for three APs, gives CCK+BC to PC EPI onsets at the 2nd to 4th AP (median 2.0, 10 of 10 pairs; 3.5 with the reconstruction scaled to the authors' amplitudes); rule (b) gives the 1st AP in every pair (median 1.0). Expected 10 to 12. Under both rules all 6 CCK+BC to PC pairs with trains also have an onset in some 10-AP train (the 160 Hz train in all 6), where the criterion needs none. The rules mark release in 6 of 7 PV+BC and 8 of 8 AAC to PC pairs under EPI (rule b, all of them), which the paper calls synchronous, so they do not appear to be the authors' procedure; this is asked of a reader, and how the onset was found is a question for the paper's authors (findings). The _EPA tables carry an undocumented code AR from some AP on in every CCK+BC and CCK+DTI to PC EPI table and in no PV+BC or AAC table; read as the onset, it gives a CCK+BC median of 12 (quartiles 10 to 12.8, range 8 to 19) against the paper's 11 (10 to 14, range 10 to 19), and no AR in any CCK+BC 10-AP train. It is not a rule of the claims file and is shown only.
deviations: Template from the average of the 11th IPSCs of the pair's trains; four CCK+BC pairs without trains use the single AP before EPI, and two CCK+BC pairs have no EPI recording.
100 Hz low-pass as a fourth-order zero-phase Butterworth filter, the claims file's standard choice.

Of the two pairs that transmit only under EPI, Pair07 depresses at the 34th AP (0.173, M4 b) and Pair06 does not (1.012, M4 b; under M4 a the 34th AP has no amplitude, and the last AP with one is 0.584 and 3.675).

outcomes.notes: Onset rules as fig6-cckbc-async-onset. The CCK+DTI to PC EPI median onset is 3.0 under rule (a) (5 of 7 pairs; two pairs have a template at a bound of the fit and no reconstruction; 4.5 with the authors' amplitudes) and 1.0 under rule (b), against 7 (6.3 to 7.7). At 160 Hz rule (a) gives onsets at the 2nd, 7th and 2nd AP (median 2.0, reading a of the trains) and rule (b) the 1st in all 4 pairs, against 6 to 8. No CCK+DTI to PC pair has a 320 Hz train, so reading b of the trains cannot be computed. The CCK+DTI EPI median is not below the CCK+BC one under any rule (3.0 against 2.0, 4.5 against 3.5, 1.0 against 1.0). The authors' AR marks give an EPI median of 8 (quartiles 7 to 9, range 5 to 10) against the paper's 7 (7 to 9, range 7 to 13), and 6 to 8 at 160 Hz (4 pairs) against 7 (6 to 8); shown only.
deviations: No CCK+DTI to PC pair was recorded with a 320 Hz train.

outcomes.notes: Window after the 10th AP of the 160 Hz train (the first run measured it after the isolated 11th AP, an error the verifier found). CCK+BC to PC pairs carry more charge in the 500 ms after the last EPI AP than after the 160 Hz train, but not significantly (reading a, delayed asynchronous charge, 4.44 against 1.18 pC; reading b, area under the mean trace, 4.67 against 1.61 pC; Mann-Whitney p 0.0934 for both, 10 EPI and 6 train recordings), so the CCK+BC part fails under both readings. The absence parts hold under reading b (PV+BC p 0.138, AAC p 0.130, CCK+DTI p 0.649); under reading a PV+BC (p 0.0513) and CCK+DTI (p 1, 5 EPI and 3 train recordings) hold and AAC fails (p 0.0148).
deviations: Reading b measures the area from the pre-stimulation baseline; the sweeps end before an equal window at least 500 ms after the stimulation, the paper's reference for the total charge.

Over the 10 PV+BC to PV+BC pairs with a 1 Hz train (M3 b, M2 a, decay fit over 20 ms), 3 of 5 medians are within 10%; decay 3.38 ms, latency 0.687 ms and transmission probability 1.0. The rise time is faster (0.514 against 0.63 ms) and the amplitude larger (104.4 against 81.18 pA). M2 b and the 50 ms decay window give the same count; reading d (the first AP of the trains, 14 pairs) gives 2 of 5.
deviations: No PV+BC pair has a RIP recording, so M3 a cannot be run; 14 pairs in the data set against 16.

outcomes.notes: The CCK+BC to CCK+BC and CCK+DTI to CCK+DTI pairs were recorded only with 10, 40 and 160 Hz trains; there is no RIP recording and no 1 Hz train, so none of the criterion's single-AP readings (M3 a to c) can be run. Reading d, the first AP of each train at 40 Hz or slower, is shown in the notebook and does not decide; under it at most 2 of 9 medians are within tolerance (1 under M2 a, 2 under M2 b), CCK+BC pairs have a lower transmission probability than PV+BC pairs (corrected p 0.00164) and not a longer latency (corrected p 1). Reading d is doubtful here; one CCK+BC pair has a latency of -0.12 ms and the CCK+DTI amplitudes are 2.7 to 14.2 pA.

As fig8-cck-pairs-uipsc; no single-AP recordings of the CCK+ pairs. Under reading d, shown only, CCK+BC pairs rise more slowly than CCK+DTI pairs (1.43 against 0.82 ms, corrected p 0.514 under M2 a), the opposite of the claim.

Over 10 to 14 PV+BC to PV+BC pairs per frequency, the median relative amplitude at the 10th AP is below 1 at all eight frequencies (0.806 at 1 Hz to 0.14 at 320 Hz, M4 a), and the mean of APs 2 to 10 falls with frequency (Spearman rho -0.737, p 2.4e-18). M4 b and the variant without the first three sweeps agree (rho -0.83, -0.70).

With the authors' success tables (M2 a), the median transmission probability at 80 Hz is 1 at every AP (expected 0.9 plus or minus 0.09 at the 10th). At 160 Hz it falls by 5, 10 and 5% at the 8th to 10th AP (mean 6.7%, inside 4.5 to 11). At 320 Hz it is 1.0 at the 3rd AP and 0.8 to 0.9 from the 4th to the 10th (median 0.85), so the 3rd AP is outside 0.72 to 0.99. Below 80 Hz and at every 11th AP the median is 1. Detection on the raw traces (M2 b) gives 1 at 80 Hz and 0.1 to 0.6 over the 3rd to 10th AP at 320 Hz. Neither the 80 Hz nor the 320 Hz part holds, so the outcome is not partial.
deviations: For M2 b in the trains, a uIPSC is a peak after the AP (to the next AP, at most 8 ms) above the current just before it by more than 3 SD of the 10 ms before the first AP, a standard choice.

outcomes.notes: The median 11th over first IPSC is 0.61 to 0.71 at every frequency from 5 to 320 Hz (M4 a), below 1, and does not depend on the frequency (Kruskal-Wallis p 0.124; Friedman over 10 pairs with all seven frequencies p 0.115). Under M4 b p 0.668 and 0.708.

Onset rules as fig6-cckbc-async-onset, on the 10-AP trains cut at the 10th AP. The CCK+ to CCK+ pairs have only 10, 40 and 160 Hz trains, so the two readings of which trains count select the same trains. Both rules mark asynchronous release in all 9 pairs with a train at 40 Hz or above (100%, against 45 to 66%), rule (a) at the 2nd to 5th AP at 160 Hz and rule (b) at the 1st; no pair is purely synchronous. The facilitation part holds; every pair has a relative amplitude above 1 at some AP of its 10 or 40 Hz train (largest 1.05 to 12.46 under M4 a, 1.39 to 5.71 under M4 b). The _EPA tables of these pairs carry no AR mark.
deviations: 10 CCK+ to CCK+ pairs in the data set; one CCK+BC pair (Pair01) has only a 10 Hz train, which leaves the paper's nine.

outcomes.notes: Under M4 a the median over CCK+ to CCK+ pairs of the mean relative amplitude of APs 2 to 10 is 1.559 at 10 Hz (6 pairs) and 2.153 at 40 Hz (9 pairs); at 160 Hz 5 pairs are above 1 and 4 below (median 1.191). Without the first three sweeps 1.771 and 1.497, and 6 above and 3 below at 160 Hz; under M4 b 1.558 and 1.825, and 4 above and 5 below.

outcomes.notes: All 9 pairs count as asynchronous under both rules (fig10-cck-cck-heterogeneity). No pair has its onset after the 5th AP at both 40 and 160 Hz with none at 10 Hz (0 of 9 under both rules; at least 80% needed). The durations of delayed release at 160 Hz are 24.0 to 222.4 ms over the 9 pairs (the values given as measured), 4 of 9 within 62.8 to 373.6 ms; over all trains they depend on the frequency (Kruskal-Wallis p 0.000884, medians 0, 0 and 53.5 ms at 10, 40 and 160 Hz), against the paper's independence. The total charge depends on the frequency (p 0.0444; medians 0.358, 0.749 and 2.891 pC), as stated, over 10 to 160 Hz only, as there is no 320 Hz train.
deviations: Duration of delayed release, the time from the 10th AP until the 100 Hz low-pass residual returns within 2 SD of its baseline, the criterion's standard choice.
Total charge measured from the pre-stimulation baseline; the sweeps end before an equal window at least 500 ms after the train.

outcomes.notes: The CCK+ to CCK+ pairs have no 320 Hz train, so the parts that compare 320 Hz with 40 Hz (immediate charge) and with 160 Hz (delayed charge) cannot be computed. The other parts were computed over the 9 pairs that both onset rules mark as asynchronous, and hold; the median immediate charge over APs 5 to 10 rises from 0.037 pC at 10 Hz to 0.371 pC at 40 Hz (0.837 pC at 160 Hz), and the median delayed charge rises from 0.012 to 0.102 to 1.319 pC at 10, 40 and 160 Hz.

For PV+BC to PV+BC (14 connections), PV+BC to PC (6) and AAC to PC (8) the lowest BIC is the UDR depressing model under both readings, and adding facilitation to it lowers the error by 4.1, 0.1 and 7.9% (reading a; 1.3, 2.2 and 7.1% under b), less than 10%. The SSE decrease with UDR is 22.9, 13.1 and 24.7% under reading a (17.0, 8.2 and 21.2% under b), against 35, 22 and 34%, outside tolerance. Under reading a the BIC ranking holds and the decreases lie in 10 to 50%, the criterion's partial. With other seeds of the starting points one fit stops at a worse optimum (seed 2, PV+BC to PV+BC under a; decrease 4.5% and lowest BIC UDR with facilitation); keeping the best of 16 starting points gives the numbers above.
deviations: Four starting points per fit (a standard choice); the optimizer is trust-region least squares. The notebook repeats the fits with three more seeds and keeps the best of the 16 starting points as a check.

findings.statement: The stimulation timings in the data differ from the data descriptor and the paper. RIP bursts are four APs 4.5 ms apart (222 Hz), not 160 Hz; the EPI burst is 30 APs 6.7 ms apart (147 Hz) and four 3.3 ms apart (303 Hz), not 160 and 320 Hz; the single AP precedes the RIP and EPI bursts by 1.3 s, not 1 s. The 10-AP trains are at their nominal rates.

Experiments_description.txt mislabels two recordings (PV+BC to PV+BC pair 10 s130807-0205, listed as 5 Hz, and CCK+DTI to PC pair 5 s150222-0305, listed as 40 Hz, are 10 Hz trains), names eight files that are not in the zip (three misdated s1508.. for s1308..), lists one file for two protocols in two pairs, leaves 20 recordings of the zip unnamed, lists no PV+BC to AAC pairs, and numbers the IN to PC pairs differently from the PairNN folders.

Three recordings have a header but no sweeps (CCK+BC to PC Pair07 s140616-0105 and -0106, CCK+DTI to PC Pair01 s150119-0104), three have sweeps but no _EPA table, and the RIP recording listed for PV+BC to PC pair 4 is absent. The data set holds 7 PV+BC, 8 AAC, 12 CCK+BC and 7 CCK+DTI to PC and 14 PV+BC to PV+BC pairs, fewer than the paper's 8, 9, 14, 8 and 16. The CCK+ to CCK+ pairs were recorded only with 10, 40 and 160 Hz trains, with no RIP recording, 1 Hz train or 320 Hz train, so their single-AP uIPSCs (Fig. 8) and 320 Hz charges (Fig. 10B) cannot be measured.

The current-step recordings (Fig. 2, Tables 1 and 2), the connectivity tests with unconnected pairs (Fig. 3, Table 3), the spontaneous IPSCs (Fig. 12) and the field potential and optogenetic recordings (Fig. 13A, C) are not in the data set, which is described as holding the paired recordings only.

The _EPA tables use a code AR, not described in the descriptor, that cuts off the mean row of every CCK+BC and CCK+DTI to PC EPI table and four CCK+DTI to PC 160 Hz tables from some AP on; its position matches the onset of asynchronous release the paper reports. The block the descriptor calls Relative ampl. holds amplitudes in pA.

The pairs are not labelled by pipette solution (high KCl, or low KCl with CsCl), which the paper's comparisons of Figure 7 need, and the order of the recovery intervals across sweeps, and which _EPA block holds which interval, are not documented (the AP times show 1200 down to 50 ms).
The files carry no animal or slice identifiers; the recording day in the file name is the only grouping above the pair, so results cannot be broken down by animal.

Two _EPA tables (CCK+BC to PC s140619-0204 and s140619-0105) hold column labels in place of the mean values; several tables list fewer sweeps than the raw data without a note (for example PV+BC to PC s140603-0406, 14 of 20); some have blank amplitude cells; four AAC to PC tables have successes with amplitude 0 or failures with an amplitude; a few mean rows differ from the mean of their own per-sweep values (up to 38 pA).

The Results say seven of eight CCK+DTI to PC pairs did not transmit for a single AP or an AP after RIP, and also that four of eight responded at 1 to 40 Hz or to RIP. In the data set four of the seven CCK+DTI pairs have RIP recordings and transmit to the single AP before RIP.

Question for the authors. How was the onset of asynchronous release determined (Results, Transmission of CCK+ cells, onset between the 10th and 19th AP)? Both rules the claims file names, a charge threshold on the reconstructed asynchronous current and a failure to return to baseline, mark early asynchronous charge in PV+BC and AAC pairs that the paper calls synchronous, and in the 160 Hz trains of nearly every pair. Does the AR code in the _EPA tables mark the onset, and by what criterion?

Question for the authors. Which APs gave the single-AP uIPSCs of the CCK+ interneuron pairs (Fig. 8)? The data set holds only 10, 40 and 160 Hz trains for these pairs; this attempt shows the first AP of each train at 40 Hz or slower and blocks the claims, as the claims file's readings need a RIP recording or a 1 Hz train. Which windows were used for the baseline, the peak and the single-exponential decay fit of the averaged uIPSCs?

Question for the authors. How was the recovery half-time of PV+BC to PC IPSCs (Fig. 13B) fitted; with the plateau fixed at full recovery or free, and is the value tau or tau ln 2? Only the free-plateau fits come near 495.8 ms here.

entries.name: crcns-hc-7-kohus-2016
entries.title: Inhibitory synaptic dynamics of CA3 PV+ and CCK+ interneurons (Kohus et al. 2016)
entries.description: Tests the paired-recording findings of Kohus, Kali, Rovira-Esteban, Schlingloff, Papp, Freund, Hajos and Gulyas (2016) on CRCNS data set hc-7, which holds the raw sweeps and the authors' amplitude and success tables of 60 interneuron to pyramidal cell and interneuron pairs under trains, RIP, EPI and recovery protocols. It compares uIPSC kinetics between connection types, short-term plasticity, recovery, asynchronous release and the fits of four short-term plasticity models. The current-step, connectivity, spontaneous IPSC and field potential data of the paper are not in the data set.
